dct_description_sm: The eiders that migrate through northwest Alaska nest at dispersed locations across northern Alaska and Canada. Because they are widespread it is difficult to get a good population estimate. Most of the population, however, migrates near Barrow during the spring and then again in the summer/fall. We counted eiders and other birds as they migrated past Barrow.  King (Somateria spectabilis) and Common (Somateria mollissima) eiders are important subsistence species in Alaska, Canada and Russia, yet relatively little was known about their population size, trends, movements or breeding biology. The NSB initiated studies in the 1990's to help fill these data gaps.
dct_title_s: Eider Population Monitoring, North Slope, Alaska
